# refactor(domain): assign error ownership by meaning

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**:
everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to
any other issue or pull request.

Lands after two earlier issues and builds on both: the one that splits config I/O from config
policy, and the one that moves `messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` into `src/failures/`.
Check that `src/failures/` exists before you start; if it does not, stop and say so.

## What

Every kind of failure jig reports has a clear owner. Users see the same error messages, and the
same failures are retried, blocked or fatal.

## Why

All failures live in one domain file. Business code therefore appears to depend on storage, Git and
configuration details, and each new failure type adds to a single global list.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `failures` (failure presentation, unwrapping and retry execution),
`ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and policy), `flow`/`steps`
(workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting), `adapters` (Git, files,
containers, terminal, logging), `integrations/github`, `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

Read these sections of `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`: "Target responsibilities" and "Error
ownership and technical failure handling". Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow the spec
and say so in the PR.

## Target

`src/domain/errors.ts` holds the `JigError` union, `FailureKind`, `isTransient`, `isJigError` and
21 error classes. Move each class to the owner of the condition it describes, split
`ConfigInvalid` by meaning, and replace `JigError` with narrow contracts. Do the two required first
steps below before moving any class.

**Out of scope:** `messageOf`, `rootCause`, `retryResult` and `RetryPolicy`. They already live in
`src/failures/`; import them from there and do not move, wrap or inject them.
`src/integrations/github/errors.ts` holds GitHub-specific errors; leave them for the GitHub issue
unless a shared class is involved.

### Step 1 (required first): find every place an error tag is read, shown or stored

Each class split out of `ConfigInvalid` gets its own tag (see `ConfigInvalid` below). Before
changing any tag, grep `src/` for every read of `_tag`, every match on the string `'ConfigInvalid'`,
every `instanceof` or class-name check, and every place an error is serialized or logged. For each
one, decide whether a tag change there is visible to users or breaks stored data, and put the list
in the PR. An earlier read-only investigation found the following; confirm it against the code as
it stands, since lines may have moved.

Production code that reads a jig error tag. None of these involve `ConfigInvalid`, so the split
does not affect them:

- `src/adapters/git/remote-ref.ts:57` retries when `_tag === 'RemoteUnavailable'`.
- `src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:137,140` retries and recovers on
  `_tag === 'RunStateConflict'`.
- `src/integrations/github/octokit-github.ts:62` and `implement-issue.ts:473` match GitHub's own
  tags (`GithubUnavailable`, `GithubRefused`).
- `src/config/presets.ts:51` switches on `PresetSourceFailure` tags.
- `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:311-320` reads sandcastle's own failure tags to
  decide between `ConfigInvalid` and `SandboxUnavailable`. That tag set belongs to the library.
  The class it produces changes; nothing reads jig's tag there.

No production code compares against the string `'ConfigInvalid'` or uses
`instanceof ConfigInvalid`. Classification uses `kind` (`src/flow/engine.ts:226`), not the tag.

Surfaces that show or store errors:

| Surface | What it carries | Tag change visible or breaking? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI output and exit code (`src/cli/with-error-handling.ts:22`) | an `Err`'s `message` only; every `Err` exits 1 | No |
| Saved run state, local and remote (`blockedReason`, `src/flow/engine.ts:227`) | the error's `message` | No |
| Run events and metrics log (`reason` in `src/domain/events.ts`, `src/observers/metrics.ts:27,86`) | the error's `message` | No |
| GitHub orchestration state and comments (`src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:159`) | statuses and receipts, no errors | No |
| Telemetry (`src/observers/tracing-observer.ts:31,81`) | span status message from `reason` | No |
| Logs written with `{ err }` (`src/app/report-cleanup.ts:12`, `src/app/observed-events.ts:13`, `src/app/throwaway-sandbox.ts:61`, `src/adapters/sandcastle/sandcastle-session.ts:342,370`) | pino's error serializer writes `type` (the constructor name), `message`, `stack` and own fields, including `_tag`; `TaggedError` also sets `name` to the tag, so the stack starts with it | Visible in the console and the run's JSON log file, but only as diagnostics: nothing in jig parses them, and `type` changes with the class anyway |
| Specs | 56 `toBeInstanceOf(ConfigInvalid)` assertions across 22 spec files; `src/domain/errors.spec.ts:105` asserts `_tag === constructor.name` for every class | Instance assertions must name the new classes. The tag-equals-class-name test already requires distinct tags; keep it and extend it to the new classes |

Conclusion of that investigation: **no surface needs a compatibility translation.** Log lines show
the new tags, and that change is accepted. If you find a surface that shows the tag to users as
part of a stable output, or stores it in data that jig reads back, keep compatibility at that one
point with an explicit translation from the new tag to `'ConfigInvalid'`, and name it in the PR.

### Step 2 (required early): move retry-policy assembly from domain to flow

Retry counts and delays are technical policy, not business rules. Step retry has three owners:

- Config owns the defaults: `STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `STEP_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000` in
  `src/config/load-config.ts`, copied by `runSettingsFrom` into `RunSettings.maxStepRetries` and
  `retryDelayMs`. Leave them there. Domain keeps the resolved `RunSettings` type.
- Classification stays with the errors: each class keeps its literal `kind`, and domain keeps
  `FailureKind` and `isTransient` as a plain rule (see "Classification" below).
- Flow owns assembling the `RetryPolicy`, because flow makes the step retry decision.

Today `transientRetryPolicy(settings: RunSettings)` returns
`{ retries: settings.maxStepRetries, delayMs: settings.retryDelayMs, shouldRetry: isTransient }`,
and its consumers are `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts`. The earlier helper move may
have left it in `src/domain/retry.ts` with a structural result type that copies `RetryPolicy`'s
shape so domain need not import `failures`. Check where `transientRetryPolicy` and its result type
live when you start, and move them from there:

- Put the builder in flow, for example `src/flow/retry-policy.ts`. It imports `RetryPolicy` from
  `src/failures/retry.ts` and returns that type, not a lookalike.
- `src/flow/engine.ts` imports it from flow. `src/app/container.ts` imports it from flow too; the
  owner table allows app to import flow.
- Remove the builder and the structural lookalike type from domain. Delete `src/domain/retry.ts`
  if nothing is left in it.
- Move its specs with it. Same retries, same delays, same retryable kinds. No new settings.

### Proposed owners — verify each against its callers

A starting proposal from an earlier inventory. Every class in this table keeps its tag, message
and literal `kind`; only the classes split out of `ConfigInvalid` below get new tags. Check each row against the actual constructors and consumers; where a caller shows a
different meaning, follow the caller and record why in the PR.

| Error | Owner | Extra fields | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AgentRunFailed` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `AgentOutputInvalid` | `ports/agent-session` | — | retry |
| `PlanNotCovered` | `domain/errors` | — | retry |
| `DesignUnresolved` | `domain/errors` | `findingIds` | block |
| `RemoteUnavailable` | `ports/git` | — | retry |
| `SandboxUnavailable` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | retry |
| `SetupCommandFailed` | `ports/sandbox-session` | `output` | retry |
| `RunStateConflict` | `ports/run-state-failures` | — | block |
| `RunCodeUnavailable` | `ports/run-code` | — | block |
| `MergeFailed` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `GitCommandFailed` | `ports/git` | `command`, `output` | block |
| `CommitImportRefused` | `ports/workspace` | — | block |
| `CommitRejected` | `ports/workspace` | `output` | block |
| `ConfigInvalid` | `config/errors`, split below | — | fatal |
| `RunRequestInvalid` | `app/run-request` | — | fatal |
| `RunInProgress` | `ports/run-lock` | — | fatal |
| `MetricsLogCorrupt` | `ports/metrics-log` | — | fatal |
| `LocalStateUnwritable` | `ports/local-state` | `path` | fatal |
| `CodexLoginNotSaved` | `ports/sandbox-session` | — | fatal |
| `ImageBuildFailed` | `ports/sandbox-images` | `output` | fatal |
| `CommandInputInvalid` | `cli/errors` | — | fatal |

Shared Git failures live once in `ports/git.ts`. Shared run-state failures live in
`ports/run-state-failures.ts`, which `run-store` and `run-code` both import, so neither imports the
other. No ports-wide error barrel and no re-exports from `domain`.

### `ConfigInvalid`

`ConfigInvalid` appears in `RunStoreFailure` (`src/ports/run-store.ts`), so moving it into config
unchanged would make ports depend on config. Keep `ConfigInvalid` in config for schema,
environment, preset and provider-selection validation only. Proposed splits for its other uses:

| Meaning today | Replacement and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid local or remote saved run; invalid state from a custom store | `RunStateInvalid`, `ports/run-state-failures` |
| Custom-store operational failure | `RunStoreOperationFailed`, `ports/run-store` |
| Loading or validating a custom-store module | `RunStoreSetupInvalid`, `app/run-stores` |
| Missing credentials, invalid selected login, credential-file access | `SandboxCredentialsInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Sandbox setup prerequisites or recipe validation | `SandboxPreparationInvalid`, `ports/sandbox-session` |
| Repository, root or branch prerequisites | `RepositoryInvalid`, `ports/git` |
| Symlink refusal and prerequisite file operations outside config sources | `LocalPreparationFailed`, `ports/local-state` |

Each replacement gets its own `_tag`, equal to its class name (`RunStateInvalid`,
`RunStoreOperationFailed`, and so on), so no two classes share a tag and a tag can be matched
exhaustively. Each keeps the message-only payload, the same message text and `kind: 'fatal'`, so
users see the same output and exit code. Use step 1's list for the tag checks, `instanceof`,
class-name checks and serialization to update; add a compatibility translation only where step 1
says one is needed. Keep the prerequisite cases that are deliberately
translated into `MergeFailed`. Config keeps its current import allowlist; adapters translate config
validation into capability failures where needed.

### Classification and workflow contracts

- Classes keep their literal `kind`. Domain keeps `FailureKind` and `isTransient`, which takes the
  structural input `{ kind: FailureKind }` instead of `JigError`. The flow retry-policy builder from
  step 2 uses it as `shouldRetry`.
- Replace `JigError` in `src/flow/define-flow.ts` and `src/flow/engine.ts` with step failures built
  from domain and port failures, plus each engine method's persistence failures. Flow must not
  import `steps` or `app` to derive these types (lint rule `flow-does-not-assemble-workflows`).
  `app` checks that the assembled workflow fits flow's contracts.
- Remove `JigError`. Define an aggregate only at an application operation that needs one, and keep
  CLI-only errors out of it.
- Delete `isJigError` and its class registry; nothing in production uses them.

## Don't undo these

- **`messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` stay in `src/failures/` as direct imports.** Do not
  add ports, adapters or injection for them. The same applies to the flow retry-policy builder: it
  is an ordinary function that engine and app import, not a port or a dependency passed in.
- Do not change construction or wiring in `src/app/container.ts` beyond import paths and types.
  The construction mechanism is decided separately.
- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged. The one tag change is the distinct tags of the
  classes split out of `ConfigInvalid`; their messages and exit codes stay the same.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- Change only what this issue needs. Leave unrelated specs and assertions as they are.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.

## Documentation

Internal-only work: no public guide changes. Update these references in place, present tense:
`docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md` (the paragraph about where classes live today, which also says
the move "keeps every tag": say instead that split classes get their own tags), and any other file
that names a moved path or `transientRetryPolicy`.

## Verification

From the repository root, with Node 26.13.0:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub.

## Done when

- [ ] The PR has a table with every error's old owner, new owner, and how its tag, fields and
      retry/block/fatal classification are kept at its consumers.
- [ ] `git grep -n -w -e JigError -e isJigError src` finds nothing.
- [ ] No two error classes share a `_tag`: every class's tag equals its class name, as
      `src/domain/errors.spec.ts` (or wherever its cases move) checks for every class, the new
      ones included.
- [ ] The PR lists step 1's tag read/show/store places and says which, if any, needed a
      compatibility translation.
- [ ] Domain exports no retry-policy builder and no retry-policy type:
      `git grep -n -E "export .*(RetryPolicy|transientRetryPolicy)" src/domain` finds nothing.
- [ ] The flow builder returns `RetryPolicy` imported from `src/failures/retry.ts`, and
      `src/flow/engine.ts` and `src/app/container.ts` import the builder from flow.
- [ ] Domain imports no capability, config or CLI error. Ports import nothing outside domain and
      ports (`npm run lint:dependencies`).
- [ ] Behavior tests show unchanged classification and messages, including retries running out and
      becoming blocked with the same count and delays, immediate blocking, fatal propagation,
      malformed saved state and original-cause reporting.
- [ ] The verification above passes.

plan.summary: Redistribute failure classes from domain to their semantic owners, split ConfigInvalid into distinct capability and application failures, replace JigError with narrow contracts, and move retry-policy assembly into flow. Preserve messages, payloads, classification, retry behavior and exit codes; only ConfigInvalid-derived classes receive new tags. The prerequisite src/failures/ exists and remains unchanged.
plan.approach: First, audit src/ for tag reads, ConfigInvalid string matches, instanceof and constructor-name checks, serialization and logging. Record each surface and compatibility decision for the PR, including container and sandbox cleanup diagnostics. Resolve one explicit request/spec mismatch during design: the request accepts changed diagnostic tags, while the spec literally requires translation wherever old tags are shown or stored. Follow the spec where they disagree and document the resolution. Before relocating classes, move transientRetryPolicy and its specs from domain/retry.ts to flow/retry-policy.ts, return the existing generic RetryPolicy from failures, update engine/container imports, and remove the structural lookalike. Keep config defaults and resolved domain settings unchanged. Inventory constructors and consumers to confirm each proposed owner, then move classes without re-exports or a ports-wide barrel. Retain PlanNotCovered, DesignUnresolved, FailureKind and structural isTransient in domain. Split ConfigInvalid into configuration validation, RunStateInvalid, RunStoreOperationFailed, RunStoreSetupInvalid, SandboxCredentialsInvalid, SandboxPreparationInvalid, RepositoryInvalid and LocalPreparationFailed; preserve existing MergeFailed translations. Define shared Git failures in ports/git and shared state failures in ports/run-state-failures. Existing boundaries currently hide capability failures inside domain and expose ConfigInvalid through RunStoreFailure; adapter translations and portable port contracts must resolve these leaks without expanding config's allowlist. Design explicit step contracts from domain/port failures and method-specific persistence contracts, with app checking workflow assignability. Remove JigError and isJigError everywhere, including CLI wrappers and GitHub orchestration; narrow those consumers without relocating GitHub-specific classes. Keep flow independent of app/steps and limit container edits to imports and types. The broader spec also targets composition extraction and GitHub redistribution, but those remain separate work. Update ownership documentation and existing dependency enforcement where necessary. Preserve classification, fields, messages and unique class-name tags through colocated tests; cover retry exhaustion with unchanged counts and exponential delays, immediate blocking, fatal propagation, malformed saved state and original-cause reporting. Prepare PR ownership and diagnostic-surface tables. On Node 26.13.0 run dependency lint, lint, typecheck, tests, build, format:check and validate -- --skip test:mutation, plus the required absence checks, without host agent execution or publication.
